data.exact_reserve_text: In 2020, there has been an overall net surplus in ultimate claims of GBP 6.0m (2019: GBP 24.6m) due to lower than expected incurred movements across most classes of business. The back years, 2017 and prior, contributed GBP 17.6m to the annual result, following better than expected reserve utilisation in the calendar year.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Expected ultimate gross loss across all years of account reported (USD figures noted) with a large proportion already incurred; favourable legal rulings reduced incurred amounts versus earlier forecasts.
Aggregate ultimate gross catastrophe losses projected (after cessions) with movements in year-end incurred; contributed materially to prior years' development analysis.
Market-wide arbitration result enabled a release from reserves of GBP 3.2m.
Better than expected performance on a large Irish motor account (written 2012-16) generated a significant portion of a GBP 6.2m gross back-year release (approximately 60%).

named_events.loss_description: Ultimate gross loss estimates reported (USD figures); syndicate ultimate gross loss estimates cited and net exposures noted; protected by surplus and excess of loss covers.
Gross ultimate provision for COVID-19 reported as $29.0m (of which a small amount was incurred at year end); noted as an evolving industry issue with potential multi-year impacts.
Expected ultimate gross loss across all years of account is reported (USD amounts). Legal rulings improved outcomes versus initial forecasts.
Roughly 10% deterioration in gross loss for Irma noted (driven by catastrophe excess of loss book), largely protected by outwards reinsurance.
Modest ongoing reserves retained on the Japanese EQ and Thai floods of 2010/11.
Included among 2017 catastrophes with projected ultimate gross losses reported for the group of events.

data.standardized_narrative: Using the gross claims development triangle, the syndicate shows a small net gross strengthening of reserves in 2020 of approximately GBP 1.3m (c.0.4% of opening gross claims outstanding), driven by adverse movements in certain more recent underwriting years (notably 2016-2018) that offset releases in older years. The managing agent describes overall favourable incurred movements across most classes (a reported net surplus on an after-reinsurance basis), with prior-year activity (2017 and prior) also contributing to the calendar year result through reserve utilisation and specific releases (e.g. arbitration and improved motor performance). Key underlying drivers cited include favourable claims development, selected large-loss movements and continued monitoring of COVID-19 exposures.
raw_causal_phrases: lower than expected incurred movements across most classes of business
better than expected reserve utilisation in the calendar year
there was a GBP 6.2m gross back-year release, 60% of which was generated by a better than expected performance on the large Irish motor account
a gross back-year release of GBP 16.1m
a positive run-off of GBP 16.1m on the 2017 and prior years' reserves
the back years, 2017 and prior, contributed GBP 17.6m to the annual result

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development (PYD) calculated from the gross claims development triangle (gross figures) by comparing the current estimate to the previous diagonal for underwriting years 2011-2018. The report also states an overall net surplus of GBP 6.0m (net of reinsurance) which conflicts with the small gross strengthening derived from the triangle; the narrative net figure appears to be after reinsurance. The triangle is presented in GBP '000 and has been converted to millions. '2010 and prior' aggregate column was excluded per instructions. Some event impacts in the text are reported in USD and were not converted; amounts in prior_year_events are given only where GBP figures were explicitly stated.
